questions.q: Let x1,x2,…,x11 be 11 distinct positive integers. If we replace the largest of these integers by the median of the other 10 integers, then
questions.solution:
Let the given 11 distinct positive integers are in increasing order x1,x2,x3,x4,x5,x6,x7,x8,x9,x10,x11, so x11
is largest of these integers and the median is x6. Now, median of first 10 numbers is
x6+x62=m( Let )

x1,x2,x3,x4,x5,m,x6,x7,x8,x9,x10
∵ m<x6 as x5<x5+x62<x6

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In a city, the total income of all people with salary below $Rs. 10000$ per annum is less than the total income of all people with salary above $Rs. 10000$ per annum. If the salaries of people in the first group increases by $5 \%$ and the salaries of people in the second group decreases by $5 \%$ then the average income of all people
options: cannot be determined from the data
questions.solution:
Let total number of people with salary below $\mathrm{Rs. 10000}$ per annum is $x$ and salary is $A$. Let total number of people with salary above $\mathrm{Rs. 10000}$ per annum is $y$ and salary is $B$ then.
$\mathrm{xA}-\mathrm{yB} \lt  0\frac{\text { average after }}{\text { average before }}=\frac{x\left(\frac{105}{100} A\right)+y\left(\frac{95}{100} B\right)}{x A+y B}=1+\frac{5}{100}\left(\frac{x A-y B}{x A+y B}\right)$

Which of the following is necessarily true?
options: $\mu$ may or may not be equal to $\hat{\mu}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The average incomes of the people in two villages are $p$ and $Q$, respectively. Assume that $P \neq Q$. A person moves from the first village to the second village. The new average incomes are P' and Q', respectively. Which of the following is not possible?
questions.solution: Let number of peoples in two villages are $\mathrm{n}$ and $\mathrm{m}$ respectively So $\mathrm{nP}-\mathrm{P}^{\prime}(\mathrm{n}-1)=(\mathrm{m}+1) \mathrm{Q}^{\prime}-\mathrm{mQ}\mathrm{n}\left(\mathrm{P}-\mathrm{P}^{\prime}\right)+\mathrm{P}^{\prime}=\mathrm{m}\left(\mathrm{Q}^{\prime}-\mathrm{Q}\right)+\mathrm{Q}^{\prime}$

questions.q: Let $n \geq 3$.A list of numbers $x_{1}, x_{2}, \ldots \ldots \ldots x_{n}$ has mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma .$ A new list of numbers $y_{1}, y_{2}, \ldots \ldots \ldots . y_{n}$ is made as follows: $y_{1}=\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{2}, y 2=\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{2}$ and $y_{j}=x$ for $j=3,4, \ldots \ldots . n$. The mean and the standard deviation of the list are $\hat{\mu}$ and $\hat{\sigma}$. Then which of the following is necessarily true?
questions.solution: $\mu=\frac{\sum x_{i}}{n} \quad n \geq 3\sigma=\sqrt{\frac{\sum x_{i}^{2}}{n}-\left(\frac{\sum x_{i}}{n}\right)^{2}}\hat{\mu}=\frac{y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3}+\ldots \ldots+y_{n}}{n}=\frac{\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{2}+\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{2}+x_{3}+x_{4}+\ldots \ldots \ldots+x_{n}}{n}=\frac{\mathrm{x}_{1}+\mathrm{x}_{2}+\ldots \ldots . .+\mathrm{x}_{\mathrm{n}}}{\mathrm{n}}=\mu\hat{\sigma}=\sqrt{\frac{\left(\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{2}\right)^{2}+\left(\frac{x_{1}+x_{2}}{2}\right)^{2}+x_{3}^{2}+\ldots \ldots+x_{n}^{2}}{n}-\left(\frac{\sum y_{1}}{n}\right)^{2}}\begin{array}{l}=\sqrt{\frac{\frac{1}{4}\left(2 x_{1}^{2}+2 x_{2}^{2}+4 x_{1} x_{2}\right)+x_{3}^{2}+\ldots \ldots . .+x_{n}^{2}}{n}-\left(\frac{\sum y_{1}}{n}\right)^{2}} \\ =\sqrt{\frac{\frac{1}{2}\left(x_{1}^{2}+x_{2}^{2}\right)+x_{1} x_{2}+x_{3}^{2}+\ldots \ldots+x_{n}^{2}}{n}-\left(\frac{\sum x_{i}}{n}\right)^{2}} \\ \leq \sqrt{\frac{x_{1}^{2}+x_{2}^{2}+\ldots \ldots+x_{2}^{2}}{n}-\left(\frac{\sum x_{i}}{n}\right)^{2}} \\ \hat{\sigma} \leq \sigma & \ldots \ldots \ldots(2) \\ \text { by }(1) \text { and }(2)\end{array}$
